clue.text: Darcy isn't likeable, initially — Austen heroine's quandary

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma

explanation.surface: A reader's verdict on Mr Darcy as Austen's Emma wrestles with a tricky choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a predicament where every available choice looks bad, the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Attractive person sitting on bar going topless for money

indicators.note: in a down clue sitting on puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: a doll is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: going topless says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: bar is taken as the word to trim

explanation.surface: A glamorous figure perched on a bar strips off for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The American currency unit is a common word for money in general.

clue.text: Some empty cage largely reflecting what's left after death

indicators.note: reflecting means the hidden letters are read backwards, as in a mirror
some says only part of the following words is used, a hidden run of letters

explanation.surface: An empty cage largely mirrors what remains once the occupant has died.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is property handed down in a will once the owner has died.

clue.text: Amorous old drunk's high

definitions.note: high means smelly, as of meat gone off

indicators.note: drunk's means drunk is, so the words reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: An amorous old drunk is high, under the influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' poses as intoxicated but means smelly, as game left to hang is high.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat that is high has begun to go off and smells foul.

clue.text: Space entertaining Nero, primarily?

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an area is a space

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the emperor's name

explanation.surface: A venue where the emperor Nero might be entertained with games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space' does double duty as definition and as AREA; the question mark nods to Nero watching shows in an amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre's central open floor is a space where contests are held.

clue.text: Live in sin, habitually? To an extent

indicators.note: To an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A prim remark about couples who cohabit unmarried, which is only partly the case.
explanation.definitionFit: To live somewhere is to occupy or dwell in it, a plain synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Unprepared, I am quick with excuses, at heart

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
prompt means quick or immediate

indicators.note: at heart asks for the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone admits they're unready but quick to make excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech made off the cuff, without rehearsal, is extempore and unscripted.

clue.text: Virtually hot and cross after a practical joke

indicators.note: after places the cross piece behind the article
virtually means nearly all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: x is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Someone ends up hot and cross after being on the receiving end of a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank or deception played on someone for fun is a trick of this kind.

clue.text: Blair is touring a city

indicators.note: touring means going round about, so the letters of the politician's name and verb travel into a new order

explanation.surface: The former Prime Minister Tony Blair is on a visit to a city.
explanation.definitionFit: This planned modernist city is the capital of Brazil.

clue.text: People collecting old written record for religious studies

indicators.note: collecting means the people piece gathers the others inside it

parts.note: they means people in general
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Scholars gather ancient documents for their study of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic study of God and religious belief is the subject in divinity schools.

clue.text: Allowed on a lake

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether boating or fishing on a lake is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side of a cricket field is the half behind the batsman's legs, so on can mean LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allowed is permitted, and what the law permits is lawful.

clue.text: Awfully pleased about an area for walking

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the next piece
awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to find a pleasant patch of ground for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' jumbles PLEASED to ESPLADE, and 'about' wraps that around the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront promenade is a broad paved stretch made for strolling.

clue.text: Playful university teacher hugging almost every clergyman

parts.note: arch means mischievous or teasingly playful

indicators.note: hugging means the teacher's letters wrap around the next piece

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: every means each

explanation.surface: A jolly academic embraces nearly every churchman in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful' means arch as in teasing; 'almost' drops the final H, and 'hugging' has the teacher wrap around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This senior cleric in the Anglican church ranks just below a bishop and helps run a diocese.

clue.text: Police announce list of charges

definitions.meaning: the Old ... is British slang for the police force
to advertise or publicise an event in advance
a statement of what is owed, as handed over in a restaurant

explanation.surface: The police make public a list of the offences someone is accused of.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition. 'The Old Bill' is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is slang for police, a verb for advertising, and the statement of what a customer owes.

clue.text: Change article headings in Daily Telegraph to include only males

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to include means the newspaper letters go around the following pieces
headings in means the first letters of the two newspaper words

parts.note: just means only
men are males

explanation.surface: An article's headlines in the Daily Telegraph are altered so that only men feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A modification or slight alteration made to something is a tweak or change.

clue.text: Pub garden did cooked food

indicators.note: cooked suggests the words have been worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub's beer garden served up a hot meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This baked pudding of buttered stale bread and custard is a classic British dessert.

clue.text: Belong at paper, working with all the rage

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: in means fashionable, all the rage

explanation.surface: A worker belongs at the newspaper, toiling furiously.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain to something is to be connected with it or to be part of it.

clue.text: Foreman's sock?

parts.note: George Foreman was a heavyweight boxer, and a sock is a punch, so this is a boxer's upward blow, not a works foreman's garment

explanation.surface: A work foreman's item of hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: George Foreman was a world heavyweight boxing champion; 'sock' means a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: This rising punch to the chin is a boxer's blow, a fitting sock from a heavyweight.

clue.text: What gunners might do — and unsuccessful cavalry?

definitions.meaning: gunners reload their weapons once fired
horsemen beaten back would gallop at the enemy once more

explanation.surface: Artillerymen and failed horsemen alike must have another go.
explanation.walkthrough: Both readings play on 'charge': loading a gun, and a cavalry attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Reloading a gun and making a fresh assault are both a second charging.

clue.text: Arrogant about grand piano at the front

indicators.note: at the front places the piano's letter before the other pieces

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
re means about or concerning
sumptuous means grand or lavish

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of arrogance for putting a grand piano centre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand piano' looks like an instrument, but grand is a synonym and piano a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being arrogant means overstepping and taking liberties, assuming too much about one's standing.

clue.text: Regularly uproot last row to get vegetable

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the following words, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: dig up the final row to harvest a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuber is a staple root crop dug from the soil.

clue.text: The woman's supporting American doorkeepers

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the woman's piece under the American one

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American
hers means belonging to the woman

explanation.surface: A woman's people hold up the American doormen.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendants who show people to seats or guard an entrance work as door attendants.

clue.text: Husband bitten by green parrot

indicators.note: bitten by means the husband's letter sits inside the green piece, as if in its jaws

parts.note: eco is the prefix meaning green or environmental

explanation.surface: A green parrot takes a nip out of someone's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' is a verb here, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, just as a reflected sound repeats a call.

clue.text: Professional compassion reduced debts — that's lucky

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: reduced says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: pity means compassion
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A financial adviser's kindly write-down of someone's debts is a stroke of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Circumstances that are favourable and auspicious are fortunate, a looser synonym for lucky.

clue.text: Pa drops a long throw

indicators.note: drops means the next letter is let fall from the word

parts.note: to itch is to long for something

explanation.surface: Dad fumbles a long throw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pa drops a' leaves P; 'long' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a ball is to throw it, as a baseball pitcher does.

clue.text: Ruffian upset small lads

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a yob is a British word for a loutish ruffian

explanation.surface: A thug has upset some little lads.
explanation.walkthrough: Yob is British slang for a lout or hooligan; 'upset' suits a down clue, where the word is flipped upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lads are young males, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Crikey, matron shot bird!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like crikey

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in shock that the hospital matron has gunned down a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: This large dark seabird dives for fish along coasts and rivers.

clue.text: A daughter wearing the first lady's skirt

indicators.note: wearing means the first two pieces are clothed in the lady's name, which goes around them

parts.note: in the Bible Eve was the first woman

explanation.surface: A daughter puts on Eve's skirt, a fig leaf perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirt' is a verb, to go around something rather than face it.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to dodge or avoid it, a figurative sense of going around the edge.

clue.text: Tons with motive for betrayal

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for ton or tons
a reason is a motive for doing something

explanation.surface: Plenty of motive lies behind a traitor's act of betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest form of disloyalty in law.

clue.text: Setter's perhaps after spicy snacks

indicators.note: after places the setters' piece after the spicy one

parts.note: spicy food is hot
setters are breeds of dog, so 's perhaps' marks setters as an example of dogs

explanation.surface: The crossword setter, perhaps hungry, is after something spicy to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' poses as the crossword compiler but means setters, gundogs; 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages served in split rolls are a classic street snack.
